cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: I Can Handle This
cards.instruction: Perform complete emotional readiness while quietly borrowing coping strategies from every response around you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll open our audition results together. I'm ready. What's that breathing you're doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Four in, six out. It stops my hands shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My usual routine. Count us in; I'll follow your pace.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also write down who I'll call if I don't get in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. We'll make those lists next. You write first; I'll keep count.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads opening results and claims readiness; A3 takes B breathing as familiar but follows B pace; A5 incorporates the new list into A agenda and trades counting for B writing first.

responseLogic.evidence: A1 asking about the technique then A3 calling it usual is visible face-saving, not an assessment claim that A actually knew it.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains shaking management and B4 contributes another personally useful coping practice.

heightening.evidence: B4 contact-list method changes A5 planned sequence and shared roles while A treats it as natural preparation.

specificity.evidence: A1 audition results and B2 physical nerves make the task and emotional pressure clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 acknowledgment, next task and division of work keep B helping; no speech announces the combined mechanism.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 adopts B2 method and lets B set pace.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 offers another strategy after A3 uptake.
